lines: The architecture changes the moment you cross the threshold. Rough cavern walls give way to smooth geometric surfaces — perfectly angled, mathematically precise. Not carved. Grown.

The walls pulse with inner light as your Sol unit draws near. Patterns you can't read trace circuits across every surface, reacting to your presence like a living system recognizing a familiar signal.
This crypt is ancient. Far older than any human structure on Erith. Older, perhaps, than human civilization itself.
Whatever built this place understood light the way humans understand language.

A flat crystalline tablet, etched with geometric patterns that shift when you tilt it in the light. Not optical illusions — the patterns are physically changing, rearranging themselves in response to the light frequency.
You recognize some of the geometry. It matches the interference patterns your Sol unit generates. Whoever built this understood Sol-frequency light — and built an entire architecture around it.

The tablet shows a diagram: a network of nodes connected by lines of light, spread beneath a planetary surface. Each node is labeled with a geometric symbol. One symbol repeats at the largest node — it looks like a spire.
This is a map. A map of the Underlumen network. And the Spire of Vigil is one of its primary nodes.

The Array's energy readings. The Lighthouse failures. The geometric patterns in the deep caverns. It's all connected — and this crypt was built to explain the connection to anyone who could read light.
A deep resonance fills the chamber. The crystal formations embedded in the walls vibrate with a frequency you feel in your chest.
Something massive shifts in the darkness ahead. The crypt has guardians — and they are very much awake.

actions.text: You channel Sol energy into the crystal pedestal. It flares to life, light racing along geometric grooves in the floor toward the sealed central chamber.
The right pedestal ignites. Two lines of light converge on the sealed chamber between them.

lines: Both beams converge. The sealed chamber between the pedestals fills with light — and the crystal barriers dissolve.
The central pool chambers are now accessible. The geometric patterns on the walls pulse with approval, if architecture can approve.
